title: Tahini: what it is and what it provides nutritionally

seo.title: Tahini: what it is, protein, fat, fiber and minerals
seo.meta_description: Tahini is sesame-seed paste. One USDA reference provides 697 calories, 19.7 g protein, 62.4 g fat and 8.4 g fiber per 100 g; see a 30 g serving too.
seo.search_intent: Understand what tahini is and what a realistic serving contributes nutritionally

excerpt: Tahini is a paste made by grinding sesame seeds. It is highly concentrated: the USDA reference used here provides 697 calories, 19.7 g protein, 62.4 g fat and 8.4 g fiber per 100 g. In a 30 g portion, that is about 209 calories, 5.9 g protein, 18.7 g fat and 2.5 g fiber. Mineral content, especially calcium, varies substantially with seed type and hull removal.
content_html:
Tahini pours like a sauce, but nutritionally it behaves more like seed butter. It is ground sesame, so a small volume concentrates the seed's oil, protein and minerals.

What exactly is tahini?

Sesame seeds are ground until their own oil turns the solids into a fluid paste. Some products contain only sesame; others add salt or other ingredients. Hulled versus unhulled seeds and raw versus roasted processing also change flavor and composition.

What does a realistic portion provide?

The current USDA Foundation sesame-butter reference provides per 100 g about 697 calories, 19.7 g protein, 62.4 g fat, 14.2 g carbohydrate and 8.4 g fiber.

NutrientPer 100 gPer 30 g
Calories697~209
Protein19.7 g~5.9 g
Fat62.4 g~18.7 g
Fiber8.4 g~2.5 g
Magnesium357 mg~107 mg
Iron7.0 mg~2.1 mg

Thirty grams is enough to make a meaningful nutritional contribution, but it also provides just over 200 calories in this reference. That is not a reason to avoid tahini; it is a reason to count it as a substantive ingredient rather than a calorie-free condiment.

Why can calcium be much lower than expected?

This analysis contains about 116 mg calcium/100 g, far below the 975 mg in a whole dried sesame reference. Much of sesame's calcium is associated with the hull, so the seed type and degree of hulling matter.

That means a generic claim that all tahini contains nearly 1,000 mg calcium/100 g is unreliable. Product-to-product variation can be large.

The fat is mostly unsaturated

Fat is the dominant macronutrient, with mono- and polyunsaturated fats making up most of it. That natural oil is also what gives tahini its flowing texture.

How tahini fits into a meal

It adds body to hummus, lemon sauces, dressings, toast and grain bowls. A modest serving contributes protein and minerals, while a very generous pour can add several hundred calories.

The best way to judge a jar is straightforward: check the ingredient list, serving amount, and any nutrient you care about—especially calcium or sodium—on that specific product.

faq.question: What is tahini made from?
faq.answer: Ground sesame seeds, sometimes with salt or other additions depending on the brand.

faq.question: How much protein is in tahini?
faq.answer: The reference used here contains 19.7 g/100 g, about 5.9 g in 30 g.

faq.question: Is tahini high in calories?
faq.answer: Yes. It is seed butter rich in natural oil: about 697 calories/100 g and 209 calories per 30 g in this reference.

faq.question: Is all tahini high in calcium?
faq.answer: No. Calcium varies greatly depending on seed hull and processing; the USDA Foundation reference used here has about 116 mg/100 g.
